zoning_density: Cities should have to allow apartment buildings in most neighborhoods, including ones now zoned only for houses.
Neighborhoods zoned for houses should also allow duplexes and townhomes, but not large apartment buildings.
Each neighborhood should decide for itself what can be built.
Neighborhoods zoned only for single-family houses should stay that way.
zoning_state_override: States should override city zoning whenever a city falls short of its housing goals.
States should override city zoning only near public transit and job centers.
Zoning decisions should stay with cities and towns, without states overriding them.
housing_approval: Housing that meets every rule should be approved automatically, with no hearings or lawsuits to delay it.
Housing that meets every rule should be approved after a short public comment period.
Neighbors should be able to weigh in at hearings and sue over new housing, even when it meets every rule.
rent_control: Cities should be able to cap yearly rent increases for current tenants tightly, at no more than inflation.
Cities should be able to cap yearly rent increases at around inflation plus a few percent, with new buildings exempt.
Cities should limit rent increases only temporarily during emergencies.
Cities shouldn't limit how much landlords raise rent.
eviction_cause: Landlords should need a specific reason, like unpaid rent, to evict or refuse to renew any tenant.
Landlords should need a specific reason to evict or not renew tenants who've lived there a year or more.
Landlords can end a lease when its term ends, without giving a reason.
rent_vouchers: Every low-income family that qualifies for federal rent help should get it.
More families should get federal rent help than today, but not necessarily all who qualify.
Federal rent help should stay at about today's level, reaching about 1 in 4 eligible families.
Fewer families should get federal rent help, with more reliance on the private market.
public_housing: Government should build and own a large amount of housing, open to people of all incomes.
Government should build and own more housing for low-income people.
Government shouldn't own housing; it should pay private builders through tax credits to build affordable homes.
Government shouldn't build or pay for housing; leave it to the market.
encampments: People should be allowed to camp on sidewalks and in parks until there's enough shelter or housing for them.
Cities can clear camps only after offering each person a shelter bed.
Cities can ban camping and clear camps even when there aren't enough shelter beds.
Cities should ban camping and fine or jail people who don't move.
housing_first: Homeless people with addiction or mental illness should get housing first, with no requirement to be sober or in treatment.
They should get housing first, but have to accept treatment to keep it.
They should have to get sober or start treatment before getting housing.
involuntary_treatment: Treatment should stay voluntary unless a person is an immediate danger to themselves or others.
People should also be required to get treatment when they can't meet basic needs like food and shelter.
Requiring treatment should be much easier, including longer required hospital stays.
investor_homes: Large investment firms should be banned from buying single-family homes to rent out.
Large firms can buy homes to rent out, but with limits or extra taxes.
Large firms should be free to buy homes to rent out, since that adds rental housing.
short_term_rentals: Whole-home nightly rentals like Airbnb should be banned in most neighborhoods.
Short-term rentals should be allowed only in the owner's own home.
Short-term rentals should be allowed if they register and pay taxes.
mortgage_deduction: The mortgage interest deduction should end, with the money going to renters or first-time buyers.
Keep the mortgage interest deduction, but only for smaller mortgages.
Keep the mortgage interest deduction as it is.
Expand the mortgage interest deduction to help more homeowners.
transit_vs_roads: Much more transportation money should go to public transit, and less to new roads.
Somewhat more transportation money should go to public transit.
Keep about today's split between transit and roads.
More transportation money should go to roads and highways.
